q: אישה בת 84 לאחר אשפוז ותקופה ממושכת במיטה חווה ירידה בכושר ההליכה ובעצמאות במעברים ובקימה. איזה מושג מתאר את הירידה התפקודית בעקבות המחלה וחוסר הפעילות?
o: ירידה בכושר עקב מחלה וחוסר פעילות
אירוע מוחי חד עם פגיעה מוקדית חדשה
תסמונת פרקינסונית כתופעת לוואי תרופתית
מחלת כבד כרונית עם יתר לחץ דם פורטלי
explanation:
**ירידה בכושר בעקבות מחלה וחוסר פעילות** היא תרחיש מוכר לצורך שיקום בקשישים. חוזר משרד הבריאות מתאר ירידה בהליכה, במעברים ובקימה לאחר ריתוק למיטה, מחלה חריפה או אשפוז; זהו התיאור שניתן בשאלה (סעיף 5.1.4, עמ׳ 4).
"שיקום בעקבות ירידה תפקודית עקב מחלה - Deconditioning" (עמ׳ 4).

**א. ירידה בכושר עקב מחלה וחוסר פעילות.** נכונה, האפשרות תואמת את ההקשר ואת תחומי הירידה התפקודית המתוארים בחוזר (עמ׳ 4).
**ב. אירוע מוחי חד עם פגיעה מוקדית חדשה.** שגויה, הירידה שנשאלה מוגדרת בחוזר לפי ריתוק למיטה ומחלה; אין בתיאור ממצא מוקדי חדש המצדיק החלפתה באירוע מוחי (עמ׳ 4).
**ג. תסמונת פרקינסונית כתופעת לוואי תרופתית.** שגויה, התיאור תואם את הירידה לאחר מחלה וריתוק למיטה; לא ניתנה חשיפה תרופתית או תסמונת מוטורית המגדירה חלופה זו (עמ׳ 4).
**ד. מחלת כבד כרונית עם יתר לחץ דם פורטלי.** שגויה, מחלת כבד ויתר לחץ דם פורטלי אינם מתארים את תבנית הירידה בהליכה ובמעברים בעקבות חוסר פעילות המוגדרת כאן (עמ׳ 4).

מקור: משרד הבריאות, חוזר 4/2009, סעיף 5.1.4, עמ׳ 4.
ref: Hazzard Ch 55 — REHABILITATION· Harrison Ch 355 — Cirrhosis and Its Complications

q: An 84-year-old man with renal impairment, reduced fluid intake, and mild dementia develops delirium. He takes morphine and gabapentin and now has hypotension and worsening kidney function. Which approach addresses potentially treatable contributors?
o: Review medication while evaluating acute illness and fluid status
Reduce one medication and defer other evaluation pending the response
Start sedation and defer evaluation of the physical changes
Attribute the change to dementia and repeat cognitive testing later
explanation:
**Delirium often has multiple contributors**, so evaluation should combine examination, medication review, and investigations guided by the presentation. "Identifying the potentially multifactorial contributors to the delirium is of paramount importance." (p. 885). The source also states, "A complete medication review, including over-the-counter medications, is critical." (p. 885).

**A. Review medication while evaluating acute illness and fluid status.** Correct, this evaluates medication exposure alongside the new physical abnormalities, applying the source’s multifactorial approach (p. 885).
**B. Reduce one medication and defer other evaluation pending the response.** Wrong, waiting after one drug change delays the broader evaluation needed to identify other treatable contributors (p. 885).
**C. Start sedation and defer evaluation of the physical changes.** Wrong, symptom sedation does not establish the cause of the new hypotension and renal deterioration; those findings warrant medical evaluation (p. 885).
**D. Attribute the change to dementia and repeat cognitive testing later.** Wrong, the acute change requires evaluation for delirium and new illness rather than attribution to baseline dementia (p. 885).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 885.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 76-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18), BPH, and insomnia has had worsening confusion and visual hallucinations of children in his room for two months. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, terazosin 5 mg at bedtime, and diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime for sleep. Examination shows cogwheel rigidity and bradykinesia. Which change reduces the strong anticholinergic exposure identified by Beers 2023?
o: Replace diphenhydramine with doxylamine and reassess cognition.
Replace diphenhydramine with hydroxyzine and reassess cognition.
Discontinue diphenhydramine and reassess the clinical symptoms.
Continue diphenhydramine and reassess the clinical symptoms.
explanation:
**Diphenhydramine** belongs to the highly anticholinergic first-generation antihistamines that Beers advises avoiding. Confusion and cumulative anticholinergic exposure are relevant to medication review; this identifies a modifiable exposure without establishing the cause of all the patient's findings (p. 2057). "Cumulative exposure to anticholinergic drugs is associated with an increased risk of falls, delirium, and dementia, even in younger adults." (p. 2057).

**A. Replace diphenhydramine with doxylamine and reassess cognition.** Wrong, doxylamine is in the same first-generation antihistamine list, so the proposed substitution retains the identified exposure (p. 2057).
**B. Replace diphenhydramine with hydroxyzine and reassess cognition.** Wrong, hydroxyzine is also listed among the highly anticholinergic first-generation antihistamines (p. 2057).
**C. Discontinue diphenhydramine and reassess the clinical symptoms.** Correct, this removes the listed drug being used for sleep and permits reassessment of symptoms (p. 2057; application).
**D. Continue diphenhydramine and reassess the clinical symptoms.** Wrong, continuation retains exposure to the drug that Beers advises avoiding for this use (p. 2057).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2057.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: A 76-year-old community-dwelling woman restricts activity after a fall because she fears falling again. Assessment also identifies balance difficulty. Which approach follows Hazzard's discussion of fear of falling within fall prevention?
o: An exercise program incorporating cognitive behavioral principles.
Cognitive behavioral treatment delivered as a separate intervention.
A vitamin D supplementation program with laboratory follow-up.
Medication treatment for sleep with scheduled clinic follow-up.
explanation:
**Fear of falling** can restrict activity, and the source discusses combining cognitive behavioral principles with exercise and multifactorial prevention. It notes that most cognitive behavioral programs used alone have not prevented falls in people with fear of falling (pp. 636, 641). "Most cognitive behavioral programs when implemented as sole interventions have not prevented falls in people with fear of falling." (p. 641).

**A. An exercise program incorporating cognitive behavioral principles.** Correct, this incorporates the combined approach discussed for fear of falling and fall risk (p. 641).
**B. Cognitive behavioral treatment delivered as a separate intervention.** Wrong, the source reports that most cognitive behavioral programs delivered as sole interventions have not prevented falls in this group (p. 641).
**C. A vitamin D supplementation program with laboratory follow-up.** Wrong, vitamin D supplementation is not reported to prevent falls in community-dwelling older adults and does not implement the combined approach (p. 639).
**D. Medication treatment for sleep with scheduled clinic follow-up.** Wrong, centrally acting medication is associated with increased fall risk; sleep medication does not implement the combined exercise and psychological approach (pp. 639, 641).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 641, 639, 636.
ref: Hazzard Ch 43 — FALLS · Harrison Ch 26 — Neurologic Causes of Weakness and Paralysis

q: אישה בישראל עם דמנציה מתונה שמונה לה אפוטרופוס זקוקה להחלטה על המשך בירור רפואי לאחר נפילה. ניתן לברר את דעתה באמצעות הסבר מותאם. בתה מבקשת לצמצם טיפול. מה נדרש מהאפוטרופוס לפני ההחלטה?
o: לבסס את ההחלטה על שיחה עם הבת ולמסור למטופלת את התוצאה
לבסס את ההחלטה על הצעת הצוות ולדחות הסבר עד לאחר הבירור
לבסס את ההחלטה על אבחנת הדמנציה ולהשאיר את השיחה למשפחה
למסור מידע מותאם, לשמוע את דעת המטופלת ולשתפה בהחלטה
explanation:
**מינוי אפוטרופוס** אינו מבטל את החובה לשתף את האדם. כאשר ניתן לברר את דעתו, יש להסביר את מהות ההחלטה, החלופות ויתרונותיהן וחסרונותיהן, ולשמוע אותו לפני הכרעה (סעיף 67ו(א), עמ׳ 67).
"האפוטרופוס ישמע את דעת האדם שהוא אפוטרופסו, ישתפו בכל עניין והחלטה הנוגעים אליו ויתייעץ עמו, אם ניתן לברר את דעתו" (עמ׳ 67).

**א. לבסס את ההחלטה על שיחה עם הבת ולמסור למטופלת את התוצאה.** שגויה, בקשת המשפחה אינה פוטרת משמיעת המטופלת שניתן לברר את דעתה (עמ׳ 67).
**ב. לבסס את ההחלטה על הצעת הצוות ולדחות הסבר עד לאחר הבירור.** שגויה, המקור דורש מידע לצורך השתתפות בהחלטה, ולא רק לאחר שההחלטה כבר יושמה (עמ׳ 67).
**ג. לבסס את ההחלטה על אבחנת הדמנציה ולהשאיר את השיחה למשפחה.** שגויה, יכולת בירור הדעה נבחנת בהקשר ההחלטה; האבחנה כשלעצמה אינה מחליפה שיתוף (עמ׳ 67).
**ד. למסור מידע מותאם, לשמוע את דעת המטופלת ולשתפה בהחלטה.** נכונה, האפשרות משלבת את מסירת המידע ושמיעת דעתה כפי שקובע החוק (עמ׳ 67).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיפים 67ו ו־68, עמ׳ 67.

q: An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with pneumonia becomes irritable on the third hospital day, grimaces with movement, and resists care. She has moderate dementia, a positive delirium screen, and difficulty localizing her reported severe generalized pain. Temperature is 37.8°C, heart rate 102, and blood pressure 160/95. Her home medications include donepezil, amlodipine, and acetaminophen 500 mg twice daily for arthritis. While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?
o: Use a short treatment trial and reassess whether pain relief justifies continuation
Escalate beyond the recommended daily limit when the initial response is small
Continue prolonged treatment and reserve liver monitoring for another drug exposure
Reject an individual treatment trial because average trial benefits were small
explanation:
**Acetaminophen has limited average benefit in osteoarthritis**, but Hazzard allows a role for short treatment durations or when NSAIDs are contraindicated (p. 787). The source also requires attention to dose limits and monitoring: "Regular monitoring for hepatotoxicity is recommended in those with prolonged use" (p. 787). Inference: a short trial with reassessment applies the source’s limited-benefit framework without assuming that this treats every cause of the patient’s pain or delirium.

**A. Use a short treatment trial and reassess whether pain relief justifies continuation.** Correct, a short trial with reassessment fits the limited benefit and possible short-duration role described (p. 787; inference).
**B. Escalate beyond the recommended daily limit when the initial response is small.** Wrong, limited benefit is not a reason to exceed the source’s recommended daily maximum (p. 787).
**C. Continue prolonged treatment and reserve liver monitoring for another drug exposure.** Wrong, prolonged acetaminophen use itself is the indication for regular hepatotoxicity monitoring in the source (p. 787).
**D. Reject an individual treatment trial because average trial benefits were small.** Wrong, the source retains a possible role for short treatment durations despite small average benefits (p. 787).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 787.
ref: Hazzard Ch 68 — PAIN MANAGEMENT · Harrison Ch 14 — Pain: Pathophysiology and Management

q: An 82-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic cancer has lost 15% of his body weight over two months. His ECOG performance status is 2, and the oncologist recommends FOLFIRINOX. Assessment shows low grip strength of 18 kg, slow gait speed of 0.6 m/s, and a Mini Nutritional Assessment score of 19. Under the EWGSOP2 approach described in Hazzard, which additional assessment estimates the muscle-mass component needed to support a sarcopenia diagnosis?
o: Repeat bilateral handgrip testing to assess muscle strength
Perform DXA to estimate appendicular skeletal muscle mass
Repeat gait-speed testing to assess physical performance
Repeat SARC-F to assess reported functional difficulties
explanation:
The EWGSOP2 approach separates **strength, muscle mass, and physical performance**. Hazzard describes muscle mass as "confirmation of the involvement of muscle in strength loss" (p. 732), and identifies DXA as a method for estimating muscle mass (p. 735). A DXA result must be interpreted rather than treating the test order itself as a confirmed diagnosis (p. 735).

**A. Repeat bilateral handgrip testing to assess muscle strength.** Wrong, grip testing measures strength, which is already known to be low; it does not supply the muscle-mass estimate sought here (pp. 734–735).
**B. Perform DXA to estimate appendicular skeletal muscle mass.** Correct, DXA estimates muscle mass, usually appendicular lean mass, and therefore assesses the missing component (p. 735).
**C. Repeat gait-speed testing to assess physical performance.** Wrong, gait speed measures physical performance and serves as a severity measure in EWGSOP2; repeating it does not estimate muscle mass (p. 735).
**D. Repeat SARC-F to assess reported functional difficulties.** Wrong, SARC-F is a screening questionnaire about functional difficulties, not an imaging estimate of appendicular muscle mass (pp. 734–735).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 732, 735, 734.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA· Harrison Ch 79 — Infections in Patients with Cancer

q: According to Hazzard, which statement describes the use of prostate brachytherapy in relation to disease risk and prostate size?
o: Brachytherapy is generally indicated as treatment for patients who have high-risk prostate cancer.
Brachytherapy is generally used as monotherapy for patients who have a large prostate.
Brachytherapy is generally combined with external beam radiation for patients with intermediate-risk disease.
Brachytherapy is generally unsuitable as monotherapy for low-risk disease with a small prostate.
explanation:
**Prostate brachytherapy** is selected according to disease risk and prostate size. Hazzard describes monotherapy for low-risk disease with a small prostate, combination with external beam radiation for intermediate-risk disease, and poor candidacy in high-risk disease (p. 1415). "For intermediate-risk patients, brachytherapy is frequently combined with EBRT (40–50 Gy)." (p. 1415).

**A. Brachytherapy is generally indicated as treatment for patients who have high-risk prostate cancer.** Wrong, high-risk patients are described as generally poor candidates for this modality. Presenting them as the usual treatment population conflicts with that risk-based selection (p. 1415).
**B. Brachytherapy is generally used as monotherapy for patients who have a large prostate.** Wrong, the monotherapy indication specifies a small prostate, not a large one. Prostate size is part of the source’s selection criteria for brachytherapy monotherapy (p. 1415).
**C. Brachytherapy is generally combined with external beam radiation for patients with intermediate-risk disease.** Correct, the source explicitly describes frequent combination with external beam radiation in intermediate-risk disease. This is the risk group and treatment combination named in the option (p. 1415).
**D. Brachytherapy is generally unsuitable as monotherapy for low-risk disease with a small prostate.** Wrong, low-risk disease with a small prostate is the source’s stated monotherapy indication. Describing that combination as unsuitable excludes the group specifically identified for treatment (p. 1415).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1415.
ref: Hazzard Ch 90 — PROSTATE CANCER · Harrison Ch 92 — Benign and Malignant Diseases of the Prostate

q: מה מהשינויים הבאים אופייני להזדקנות נורמלית של הריאה?
o: ירידה ב- Residual volume (RV)
עליה ב- diffusion lung capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO )
עליה ב- Functional residual capacity (FRC)
ירידה ב- Residual Volume ( RV)
explanation:
The **aging lung** loses elastic recoil, traps more air, and retains a greater volume after expiration. The table lists increases in both RV and FRC; reduced gas-exchange surface area and capillary density contribute to lower DLCO (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1231, 1238).
"Air trapping (↑ RV)" (p. 1238).
"Hyperinflation (↑ FRC, unchanged or decreased TLC)" (p. 1238).

**A. Decreased residual volume (RV).** Wrong, loss of elastic recoil leaves more air after maximal expiration, so RV increases with aging (pp. 1231, 1238).
**B. Increased diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO).** Wrong, capillary loss and ventilation-perfusion abnormalities contribute to reduced diffusion capacity with age (pp. 1231, 1238).
**C. Increased functional residual capacity (FRC).** Correct, a larger lung volume at the end of ordinary expiration corresponds to the hyperinflation listed for the aging lung (p. 1238).
**D. Decreased residual volume (RV).** Wrong, this repeated option also describes residual volume, which increases through air trapping rather than decreasing (pp. 1231, 1238).

Note: The two options describing decreased RV have identical content. This duplication remains in the official wording and does not change the physiological explanation.
Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1231, 1238, Table 81-1.

explanationSource.note: Checked v74 explanation sentences use Hazzard 8e; the printed IMA 7e reference is retained.

q: איזה מהבאים לא נכלל בקריטריונים של FRIED ל-FRAILTY ?
o: ירידה לא מתוכננת במשקל
הליכה איטית
יותר משתי נפילות בחצי שנה
תשישות סובייקטיבית (EXHAUSTION)
explanation:
**Recurrent falls are not a separate Fried frailty criterion.** The five components are unintentional weight loss, weakness measured by grip strength, self-reported exhaustion, slow walking, and low activity measured by weekly energy expenditure. A count of falls is not an item in the table (Hazzard 8e, p. 620, Table 42-2).

**A. Unintentional weight loss.** Wrong, it is one of the criteria, so it is not the exception sought (p. 620).
**B. Slow walking.** Wrong, slowness is part of the phenotype and therefore not the exception (p. 620).
**C. More than two falls in six months.** Correct, the question asks what is absent from the criteria. Fall count is not included, even though falls are clinically important (p. 620).
**D. Subjective exhaustion.** Wrong, self-reported exhaustion is explicitly included (p. 620).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, p. 620, Table 42-2.

explanationSource.status: Page-backed supplemental explanation; original IMA bibliography retained.

q: בן 87, לאחר ניתוח לתיקון שבר בצוואר הירך, שואל לגבי הפרוגנוזה בעוד שנה. מה מהבאים נכון?
o: הפרעות קוגניטיביות צפויות להשתפר תוך 9-10 חודשים
שיווי משקל צפוי להשתפר תוך 3-4 חודשים
דיכאון צפוי להשתפר תוך כחצי שנה
קשיים בתפקודי הגפיים התחתונות צפויים להשתפר תוך כשנה
explanation:
**Official answer:** Depression is expected to improve within about six months; lower-extremity functional difficulties are expected to improve within about one year (IMA final answer key, May 2024, question 17).

After hip fracture, depression, cognition, and upper-extremity ADL reach peak recovery at approximately four months. Balance and gait plateau at about nine months, while complex lower-extremity and instrumental activities recover at approximately one year. This supports the one-year functional component (p. 800, Figure 53-5).

**A. Cognitive problems improve within 9–10 months.** Wrong, according to the key; the book describes peak cognitive recovery earlier, at approximately four months (p. 800).
**B. Balance improves within 3–4 months.** Wrong, according to the key; balance and gait reach a recovery plateau around nine months, later than several other domains (p. 800).
**C. Depression improves within about six months.** Correct, for scoring, because it is officially accepted. The book describes depressive symptoms lasting up to six months, while describing an earlier peak in recovery; symptom duration and peak recovery must not automatically be equated (pp. 799–800).
**D. Lower-extremity functional difficulties improve within about a year.** Correct, for scoring and supported by the slower recovery of complex lower-extremity tasks (p. 800).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 799–800. Both officially accepted answers are preserved.
keySource: IMA 2024-May Subspecialty official answer key after appeals, Q17

explanationSource.status: Official accepted answer first; separately attributed book and secondary sources.

q: מה סביר למצוא ב- EEG במטופל הסובל מדליריום?
o: האטה גלובלית עם גלי אלפא
ספייקים מרובים פוקאלים
גלים מחודדים באיזור האונה הטמפוראלית
הופעת גלים ביפאזים וטריפאזים
explanation:
The general EEG pattern is **diffuse background slowing**; Hazzard describes slowing of cortical background alpha activity (Hazzard 8e, p. 880). Epileptiform findings and triphasic waves guide investigation of the cause rather than replacing the clinical definition of delirium (Palanca et al., EEG changes, Triphasic waves, and Non-convulsive status epilepticus).

**A. Global slowing with alpha waves.** Correct, under the official key. The central point is background slowing, not increased alpha activity; see the inherited caveat below (Hazzard 8e, p. 880).
**B. Multiple focal spikes.** Wrong, this is not the general slowing pattern. Spikes require assessment for epileptic activity, which can itself alter mental status (Palanca et al., Non-convulsive status epilepticus).
**C. Temporal sharp waves.** Wrong, sharp waves warrant assessment in an epileptic context rather than describing usual diffuse slowing. Inference: temporal localization requires targeted evaluation and does not identify delirium by itself (Palanca et al., Non-convulsive status epilepticus).
**D. Biphasic and triphasic waves.** Wrong, for official scoring. Triphasic waves are not the general finding in every delirium, but do occur in moderate or severe delirium and various encephalopathies; they are not specific to liver disease (Palanca et al., Triphasic waves).

Important inherited source-versus-key note: The keyed option (A) is somewhat misleading. The classic finding is diffuse global slowing, replacing normal alpha activity (8-13 Hz) with slower theta (4-7 Hz) and delta (below 4 Hz) activity (Harrison 22e, p. 3417, as cited in the existing explanation). In other words, the background slows relative to normal alpha rather than alpha activity increasing. The option may mean that normal alpha activity is replaced and slowed, consistent with the Hazzard and Harrison discussions of delirium and altered consciousness. The Harrison attribution and numerical bands in this inherited passage were not independently reverified in this batch.
Note: The alpha wording is ambiguous, and triphasic waves can also occur in delirium; distinguish the general pattern from cause-related patterns (Palanca et al., cited sections).
Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, p. 880; Palanca BJA et al. Electroencephalography and delirium in the postoperative period. Br J Anaesth. 2017;119:294-307, cited sections, doi:10.1093/bja/aew475.

q: איזה מהשינויים הבאים בארכיטקטורת השינה נחשב פיזיולוגי בגיל המבוגר?
o: עלייה ביקיצות ליליות (Sleep Fragmentation )
עלייה בזמן שינת גלים איטיים (Slow Wave Sleep )
הארכת משך שנת REM ( Rapid Eye Movement)
קיצור זמן החביון (Sleep Latency)
explanation:
Official answer: א

Aging is associated with **sleep fragmentation** and more awakenings, reduced sleep efficiency, less slow-wave sleep and longer time to fall asleep (p. 643).

**A. Increased nocturnal awakenings and sleep fragmentation.** Correct, these are explicitly described age-related changes (p. 643).
**B. More slow-wave sleep.** Wrong, slow-wave sleep decreases with age, rather than increasing (p. 643).
**C. Longer REM sleep.** Wrong, the evidence for age-related REM-duration changes is inconsistent; prolongation is not established like sleep fragmentation (p. 643).
**D. Shorter sleep latency.** Wrong, sleep initiation takes longer with aging, contrary to this option (p. 643).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 643.

q: בן 78, עם סרטן ערמונית מתקדם גרורתי, הוגדר כסופני (בשבועיים האחרונים לחייו). סוכם עם בני משפחתו על טיפול תומך בלבד. באשפוז נכנס לדליריום היפראקטיבי עם סימני אי-שקט פסיכומוטורי. טיפול ב- HALOPERIDOL לא עזר. מה הגישה לגבי טיפול בבנזודאזפינים במצב זה?
o: יש להימנע מטיפול בבנזודאזפינים מאחר שמחמירים דליריום
מומלץ שימוש בתרופות מסוג בנזודאזפינים ארוכי טווח כגון DIAZEPAM
יש להימנע ככל הניתן ממתן בזריקות ולהתמקד במתן פומי
מומלץ טיפול בבנזודיאזפינים קצרי טווח כגון MIDAZOLAM עם אפשרות טיטרציה
explanation:
In a dying patient with hyperactive delirium unresponsive to haloperidol, the goal is **relief of distress**, not necessarily preservation of alertness. When end-of-life sedation is indicated, the source recommends a short-acting agent that can be titrated to effect and goals of care; it describes oral, intravenous or subcutaneous lorazepam according to the patient's needs (p. 890).

**A. Avoid benzodiazepines because they worsen delirium.** Wrong, despite the risk of worsening confusion, sedation may be needed for severe agitation at the end of life in accordance with goals of care. Blanket avoidance misses this exception (p. 890).
**B. Use long-acting benzodiazepines such as diazepam.** Wrong, long duration does not match the preference for a short-acting agent whose effect can be adjusted (p. 890).
**C. Avoid injections whenever possible and focus on oral treatment.** Wrong, the source also describes intravenous or subcutaneous sedation and does not require an oral preference in every such case (p. 890).
**D. Use a short-acting benzodiazepine such as midazolam with titration.** Correct, officially accepted. The short-acting, titratable-agent principle is supported, but the book's named example is lorazepam; this page is not direct support for the specific midazolam recommendation (p. 890).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 890.
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An older adult has a fall without physical injury but becomes afraid of falling again. Which consequence of this fear is described in Hazzard?
o: Avoidance of daily activities helps preserve mobility during recovery.
Lack of physical injury protects against subsequent fear-related frailty.
Restriction of daily activities improves balance by increasing rest.
Avoidance of daily activities reduces mobility and contributes to frailty.
explanation:
**Fear of falling** is clinically important even after a fall without physical injury. Avoidance of daily activities can reduce mobility and promote frailty, so the consequences of a fall extend beyond fractures or bruises (p. 633).
"Falls that do not result in physical injuries can also have serious consequences including significant fear of falling" (p. 633).
"which can lead to reduced mobility and frailty through the avoidance of daily activities." (p. 633).

**A. Avoidance of daily activities helps preserve mobility during recovery.** Wrong, Avoiding daily activities is the pathway linked to reduced mobility and frailty, not preservation of mobility (p. 633).
**B. Lack of physical injury protects against subsequent fear-related frailty.** Wrong, The absence of physical injury does not remove the risk of fear-related activity restriction and frailty (p. 633).
**C. Restriction of daily activities improves balance by increasing rest.** Wrong, Fear-related avoidance reduces activity; the source links it to poorer mobility rather than improved balance through rest (p. 633).
**D. Avoidance of daily activities reduces mobility and contributes to frailty.** Correct, Fear can lead to avoidance of daily activities, reduced mobility and frailty despite the absence of physical injury (p. 633).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 633.

q: A robust older adult falls on an icy path, while an older adult with very poor physical abilities falls in a relatively hazard-free home. Which interpretation fits Hazzard?
o: Greater environmental demands are better tolerated as physical ability decreases.
Lower environmental demands make falls more likely in robust people.
Physical ability becomes less relevant as environmental demands increase.
Environmental demands interact with physical ability in determining fall risk.
explanation:
**Environmental challenge and physical ability interact** in determining fall risk. A robust person can tolerate more challenge but may still fall on an icy path, whereas very poor physical ability permits falls even in a relatively safe environment (p. 636).
"The interaction between an older person’s abilities and their exposure to environmental factors is particularly important." (p. 636).
"People with high physical abilities can withstand a bigger range of environmental challenges without falling" (p. 636).

**A. Greater environmental demands are better tolerated as physical ability decreases.** Wrong, The source describes the opposite relationship: high physical ability permits a wider range of environmental challenges, while very poor ability permits falls in safe settings (p. 636).
**B. Lower environmental demands make falls more likely in robust people.** Wrong, A relatively undemanding environment can be managed even by people with lower abilities; the page does not describe reducing demands as making robust people more likely to fall (p. 636).
**C. Physical ability becomes less relevant as environmental demands increase.** Wrong, The capacity to withstand greater challenges depends on physical ability; increasing demands does not make that ability less relevant (p. 636).
**D. Environmental demands interact with physical ability in determining fall risk.** Correct, The relation between ability and environmental challenge explains both a robust person falling on ice and a severely impaired person falling in a safe home (p. 636).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 636.

q: A patient has progressive disinhibition, apathy and loss of empathy, but an early MMSE score remains within normal limits. Which diagnostic approach is supported by Hazzard’s discussion of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia?
o: Use the normal MMSE to set aside concern about early bvFTD
Require prominent memory loss before investigating possible bvFTD
Base the early assessment on cognitive test scores without an informant
Obtain a careful patient and informant history despite the normal MMSE
explanation:
**Early bvFTD** may chiefly affect social behavior and executive function while a brief cognitive screener remains normal. Hazzard notes that "many patients score within normal limits early in the disease" and emphasizes a "history with the patient and an informant". Thus, normal screening performance does not outweigh a progressive behavioral history (inference from the source’s screening limitation, p. 873).

**A. Use the normal MMSE to set aside concern about early bvFTD.** Wrong, A normal MMSE is specifically described as possible early in bvFTD, so it cannot justify setting aside this behavioral presentation (p. 873).
**B. Require prominent memory loss before investigating possible bvFTD.** Wrong, The source describes relative sparing of other cognitive functions in the early behavioral presentation; requiring prominent memory loss would miss the syndrome being described (p. 873).
**C. Base the early assessment on cognitive test scores without an informant.** Wrong, The source says early formal neuropsychological performance can be well preserved, emphasizing the importance of patient and informant history; relying on scores alone loses that evidence (p. 873).
**D. Obtain a careful patient and informant history despite the normal MMSE.** Correct, This follows the source’s emphasis on the history and respects the limited value of the MMSE for early bvFTD (p. 873).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 873.
